options: The requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving an information security management system (ISMS)
A file format for data exchange
questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 27001 is an international standard specifying the requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving an ISMS.

questions.stem: What does the CIA triad refer to in the context of ISO/IEC 27001?
options: Confidentiality, integrity and availability of data
questions.explanation: From a data perspective, ISO/IEC 27001 is pivotal to ensuring the confidentiality, integrity and availability (CIA) of data.

questions.stem: What is described as the foundational aspect of ISO/IEC 27001?
options: The systematic assessment of information security risks
questions.explanation: The foundational aspect is the systematic assessment of information security risks: identifying threats, assessing vulnerabilities and evaluating risk impacts.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of data classification under ISO/IEC 27001?
options: To sort data alphabetically for retrieval
To decide which database vendor to use
To assign storage tiers by file size
To group data by department for billing
To classify data by sensitivity and importance so that more sensitive data receives higher levels of protection
questions.explanation: Data is classified according to its sensitivity and importance, which influences how it is handled, stored and transmitted.

questions.stem: On which principle does ISO/IEC 27001 base the limiting of access to data?
options: The principle of first come, first served
questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 27001 highlights limiting access to data based on the principle of least privilege, so only authorised individuals can access or modify data.

questions.stem: Which control makes data unreadable to unauthorised parties, both at rest and in transit?
questions.explanation: Encrypting data at rest and in transit makes it unreadable to unauthorised parties, safeguarding confidentiality and integrity.

questions.stem: What does incident management under ISO/IEC 27001 include?
options: Detecting, reporting and investigating information security incidents to mitigate their impact and prevent recurrence
questions.explanation: Organisations must have procedures for managing security incidents, including detecting, reporting and investigating them to mitigate impact and prevent recurrence.

questions.stem: What does Business Continuity Management ensure under ISO/IEC 27001?
options: That all staff receive annual bonuses
That the organisation never changes suppliers
That data is deleted after seven years
That critical data remains available or can be restored after a disruption such as a cyber-attack or natural disaster
That marketing campaigns continue during outages
questions.explanation: Business Continuity Management keeps a continuity plan including data recovery procedures so critical data remains available or restorable after a disruption.

questions.stem: Which role leads the development and implementation of the ISMS?
questions.explanation: Information Security Officers lead the development and implementation of the ISMS, ensuring controls meet ISO/IEC 27001 requirements.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the key data-related components of ISO/IEC 27001 described?
questions.explanation: The components are risk assessment, data classification, access control, encryption, incident management and business continuity; marketing attribution is unrelated.
